item.title: Xavi Espart forced off against Real Madrid as Barcelona lose another defender to injury
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 10: Xavi Espart of FC Barcelona in action during the Spanish league, LaLiga EA Sports, football match played between FC Barcelona and Getafe CF at Spotify Camp Nou stadium on October 10, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Barcelona suffered yet another injury blow on Sunday in El Clasico as Xavi Espart was forced off on the half hour mark with a problem. Espart started again at right-back for Hansi Flick’s side but picked up a knock early on after a challenge by Aurélien Tchouaméni and was replaced by Alejandro Balde. The news is another blow for Barcelona at a time when they are already without Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen and Jules Kounde due to injury. It’s also a massive setback for the teenager who has burst into the first team this season and really impressed for the Catalan giants. There’s no indication yet of how serious the problem is for Espart but we may get an update from Flick after the game. Barcelona are not due to play again until the weekend when they face Alaves in La Liga. Flick’s side then go on to face Aston Villa in the Champions League and then Atletico Madrid in La Liga.

item.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
item.description: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless Manchester derby. Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw’s second-half strike appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story. But Eva Olid’s ever-improving side fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell to her in the penalty area. That late strike saw City drop to second in the table – behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Continue reading...

item.title: Everton Eye This £25m Defender: Should Moyes Invest Despite Sale Uncertainty?
item.description: Everton Eye This £25m Defender: Should Moyes Invest Despite Sale Uncertainty? Everton have started the 2026/27 Premier League campaign with a measure of defensive discipline, although David Moyes still faces difficult decisions about the squad’s long-term balance. Eight league matches have produced two wins, four draws and two defeats, with eight goals scored and nine conceded. That record has kept the Toffees competitive, but limited squad depth leaves little room for complacency. The club currently sit ninth in the table, while uncertainty over the ownership group’s plans adds another complication to January recruitment. The Friedkin Group’s reported decision to put Everton up for sale could influence spending, particularly if prospective signings require substantial upfront fees. Moyes strengthened several areas during the summer, bringing in Brennan Johnson for a reported £22m, Merlin Röhl for £21m and Tyrique George for £18m, while Jack Grealish arrived on loan. However, Everton must balance those investments against departures, including Iliman Ndiaye’s reported £60m move to Manchester City and Beto’s £15m transfer to Fiorentina. Everton monitor Portuguese defender ahead of January According to Goodison News correspondent Scott Mason , Everton are tracking Lecce centre-back Tiago Gabriel ahead of the winter window. The report, which cites Italian transfer coverage from 4-4-2, identifies Crystal Palace, AC Milan and Roma as competing admirers of the 21-year-old. The Portuguese defender offers the aerial presence Moyes values, while he has quite efficient passing accuracy, which suggests he can contribute during possession. His season statistics reportedly include 38 clearances and two headed goals. Lecce are understood to value Gabriel at between £20.9m and £25.1m and would reject offers below that range. The Italian club have little reason to sell cheaply, particularly with several sides monitoring a young defender who could command a higher fee after further development. Everton already have James Tarkowski, Jarrad Branthwaite, Michael Keane and Jake O’Brien available at centre-back. However, Keane’s contract expires in 2027, Tarkowski is approaching the later stages of his career, and O’Brien’s limited minutes raise questions about his immediate role. Should Everton spend up to £25m on Gabriel despite their financial uncertainty? But Baltimore’s defense completely folded in the second half with no support from an offense that managed just two first downs after their first drive on the third quarter. The Bengals dropped 35 unanswered points, leading to a dismal 35-13 final result that leaves the Ravens at 4-3 heading into a tough stretch with two games against division-leading teams in the next 11 days. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to Sunday’s loss: Nikhil Mehta Jesse Minter and Anthony Weaver should have to watch that second half before every single one of their defensive meetings for the rest of the season. Allowing four straight touchdown drives out of halftime – three of at least 65 yards – is completely inexcusable for what is supposed to be one of the better defenses in the NFL. On every play, the Ravens seemed to be a second behind, unable to finish plays in the backfield or limit explosive passes over the top. Those struggles distracted from another woeful second half from an offense that simple cannot get out of its own way with procedural penalties. Vega Ioane’s knee injury also seemed to have a major impact with a steep drop-off in right guard play to Emery Jones. But regardless of his personnel issues, Declan Doyle’s inability to figure out short yardage is maddening. item.description: Subscribe to Baseball Bar-B-Cast Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube The Milwaukee Brewers have shown resilience throughout the postseason, making comeback victories a normal occurrence. On Saturday night, they did it again, just as they did against the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, erasing a 4–0 deficit, hanging on to win the game and taking a two-games-to-none lead in the World Series. On this episode of the Baseball Bar-B-Cast , Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman recap the Brewers’ comeback win in Milwaukee, which leaves them just two wins away from capturing their first-ever World Series championship. Despite Logan Henderson’s early-game struggles, the Brew Crew pitching staff did it again, with Aaron Ashby delivering heroics to help shut the door in the ninth inning, as well as Sal Frelick playing hero with the bat. Later in the show, Jake and Jordan preview Game 3, which is set to take place at Tropicana Field on Monday night, and discuss whether former Brewer Freddy Peralta can pitch the Tampa Bay Rays back into the series in a near-must-win game. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The LSU football team picked up a big win over Auburn on Saturday. The Tigers won the game, 38-17. LSU head coach Lane Kiffin gave flowers to his quarterback, Sam Leavitt, after the game. “If you look at the last two weeks, in three quarters of play, his numbers are off the charts efficient,” Kiffin said, per the school. “He was really good today.” Lane Kiffin on Sam Leavitt : “If you look at the last two weeks, in three quarters of play, his numbers are off the charts efficient.” “He was really good today.” pic.twitter.com/w6YnIIO3TW — Harrison Valentine (@HValentineLSU) October 24, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Leavitt threw for 387 passing yards on Saturday, and posted three touchdowns through the air. He added one on the ground. Leavitt helped LSU post 552 yards of total offense against Auburn. “We obviously didn’t have them ready to rock,” Auburn head coach Alex Golesh said, per the Associated Press. “Really disappointed in that. I’ll find a way to make them respond because that’s the only option they’ve got. We’ve had the high of highs, and that was the low of lows.” LSU is now 6-2 on the season, following the win. LSU got the job done against Auburn Kiffin is in his first season leading the Tigers. While LSU has lost a few games, the Tigers are currently undefeated at home this season. LSU holds a 3-2 conference mark in the SEC. Leavitt wasn’t the only star for LSU against Auburn. Tigers wide receiver Jackson Harris caught two touchdown passes. He posted nine receptions for 178 yards receiving. “He just works really hard,” Kiffin said of Harris. “We saw his speed and outran everybody in the SEC to get his play today. … It’s awesome to see.” The Tigers are about to go through a three-game gauntlet in SEC play. LSU still has to play Alabama, Texas and Tennessee in their next three contests. Time will tell if LSU can earn a bid to the College Football Playoff. The CFP is the goal for Kiffin’s program. Kiffin previously coached at Ole Miss . He led the Rebels during the 2025 season to the playoff, but left for LSU before his Rebels starting playing in the CFP. LSU football is next in action against Alabama on November 7. item.title: Jack Nicklaus predicted whether Jordan Spieth would complete the career Grand Slam in 2017
item.description: Photo by Chris Condon/PGA TOUR Jack Nicklaus has won everything there is to win in the game. And after the first three or four years of Jordan Spieth’s career, some golf fans and analysts were predicting that he could go on to match Nicklaus’ records. The Golden Bear won 73 PGA Tour events throughout his career, including a record-setting 18 major championships. Jack Nicklaus is widely considered to be the greatest golfer of all time and he is one of only six men to ever have completed the career Grand Slam. Jordan Spieth has achieved a lot in the game too, with 13 PGA Tour wins and three major championships to his name. However, the Dallas native has regressed badly over the past four years or so. He is without a major win since 2017, and he almost certainly won’t get anywhere near Nicklaus’ win tally by the time he retires. The harder Spieth works on his game, the more he seems to struggle, and his recent fall-off is genuinely hard to comprehend. After he won his third major championship at The Open in 2017, the now 33-year-old seemed to be on course to become one of the true greats of the game. And Nicklaus had full faith in his ability. Jack Nicklaus made a prediction about Jordan Spieth in 2017 Back in 2017, Nicklaus spoke about Spieth during an exhibition match at TPC Twin Cities alongside Gary Player and Lee Trevino. The Golden Bear responded when asked whether Spieth would ever complete the career Grand Slam. “ Jordan will win the PGA (Championship) whether it’s this week or another year, “ Nicklaus said. “ He’s such a good player and he has a great short game. I don’t think his long game is as good as it’s going to be. “ I think it’s going to get a lot better as he gets older. And as he gets older, he’ll solve the problems of why occasionally he’s wild. I think he’ll correct that whether that’s this week or next year or whenever it is. He’s a really good kid, and at such a young age, he’s playing great and will continue to play great. “ Unfortunately for Spieth, he has actually got worse as he has aged, unlike what Nicklaus predicted. Of course, Jordan Spieth still has plenty of time to turn things around and complete the career Grand Slam one day. However, the odds are not in his favor anymore. That in itself is hard to believe given the fact that he is only 33.

item.title: Texans tie game late to force overtime only to lose against Giants
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 25: Cade Stover #8 of the Houston Texans celebrates a two point conversion with Ed Ingram #69 of the Houston Texans during the second quarter against the New York Giants at NRG Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are seven games into the season and we are still stuck with the central question when it comes to the Houston Texans: what exactly are you? Are they a passing team that gives up fourteen penalties a game (like they did today, of which 10 were accepted)? Are they a smashmouth team with a defense that can stop anybody (except in overtime when they got absolutely steamrolled by Cam Skattebo and the Giants)? Are they good? Are they bad? Well, today’s 27-21 loss to the New York Giants, those last two questions feel pretty irrelevant. They are what they are and boy are they ever that. Texans played down to their opponents yet again, racking up 237 yards of total offense a touchdown pass to Marvin Harrison Jr. (his first with the Texans) and an Xavier Hutchinson rush are the only touchdowns the Texans could get. And the defense simply had no answers for J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo. I want you to read that statement again. The Houston Texans defense had no answers for a pretty pedestrian Giants offense; which they allowed to score 27 points and 420 yards of total offense. But most of all, we need to talk about Kamari Lassiter. Something is clearly wrong and his play has suffered as a result. Also, too, the defense is weak against explosive plays now. That’s fun. At any rate, this week is over, possibly the season, and the Texans go into their off week with way more questions in front of them than a Super Bowl caliber team should encounter at this point of the season.

item.title: Travis Kelce’s Ankle Scare Gets NFL Ruling Ahead of Seahawks Showdown
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs suffered a lot in 2025 after their star quarterback Patrick Mahomes got injured and missed the rest of the season. Chiefs just got back Mahomes and are looking to be in full swing. But in Week 5 against Los Angeles Chargers , Travis Kelce was seen limping after a tackle. At one point Kelce looked to be in discomfort. The Chargers’ defender Justin Eboigbe who delivered the tackle was expected to face some consequences. But NFL updated its weekly accountability list and now it ended up creating more controversy over this issue. NFL’s weekly accountability list creates controversy The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 22-6 at Arrowhead Stadium. The win improved the Chiefs to 5-0 while dropping the Chargers to 0-6. Kenneth Walker led the way with 128 rushing yards and two touchdowns, including a 2-yard score in the second quarter. That second-quarter touchdown play is where the controversy began. With about three minutes left in the half, Walker punched it in from short yardage. On the same sequence, Chargers defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe delivered a low hit that took Travis Kelce’s legs out. Kelce limped off the field, had his ankle taped on the sideline, but returned. He eventually finished with four catches for 53 yards as Chiefs secured the victory. Oct 4, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) walks off the field after a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Many expected that Justin Eboigbe would be fined for the tackle. But when the NFL posted its weekly accountability list of fines for the previous week’s action, Eboigbe’s name was nowhere to be found. The only Chargers player listed was Alex Harkey, fined for unnecessary roughness. A first offense for a hip-drop tackle normally carries a $17,911 fine. By leaving Eboigbe off the list, the league effectively ruled that the hit did not meet the full criteria for that violation. The NFL’s hip-drop standard requires multiple specific elements. Such as wrapping the ball carrier, swiveling, unweighting the body, and trapping the legs. Eboigbe’s contact was low and forceful enough to knock Kelce down and force him off the field temporarily. But that did not satisfy the league to trigger a fine. Despite the limping and being sidelined, Travis Kelce returned and that is a big sigh of relief for the fans. Chiefs appeared in three straight Super Bowls before 2025. Travis Kelce was limited in practice but ultimately available for the next game against the defending champions Seattle Seahawks who currently sit at 3-3. item.title: Jeff Lebby Gives Kamario Taylor Injury Update Following Early Exit vs. Oklahoma
item.description: Kamario Taylor is one of the most elite, standout players in college football right now. Playing for the Mississippi State Bulldogs football program, the quarterback has established himself as a lethal threat to opposing teams. Taylor is known for his dual-threat playmaking, and already has good stats in the 2026 season. However, he recently suffered a setback, with his team’s head coach speaking about it in detail. Jeff Lebby addresses Kamario Taylor’s injury flaring up Taylor has been performing well this season. He has recorded 1,450 passing yards with a 66.2% completion rate, 17 touchdowns, and 4 interceptions, boasting a 176.4 passer rating and an 83.3 QBR. Unfortunately, the played got himself injured in the last game. Taylor aggravated an existing right foot injury during the Bulldogs’ 23-15 loss to Oklahoma on October 24, 2026, at Davis Wade Stadium. Oct 24, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) passes the ball during warm ups prior to the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Head coach Jeff Lebby confirmed the news after the game. Speaking to the reporters after the game, he said , “On his scramble, when he took off, he felt it a little bit. So it felt like the right thing to do was to get him out of the game. Again, as we move forward, we’ll know a lot more tomorrow, we’ll know more Monday as we move through.” Taylor had also missed the previous week’s contest at LSU while dealing with the issue, which sources and reports have described as turf toe originating in the Missouri game and previously flaring up against Alabama. He was listed as questionable but cleared to start after a team decision involving the medical staff, head trainer Thomas Callans, Lebby, and Taylor himself. Lebby noted Taylor felt improved during the week, though still limited in practice. On the final play of the first quarter, Taylor scrambled from the pocket and was sacked. He immediately felt the injury and left the field. ESPN sideline reporter Tori Petry reported that Taylor could not put weight on his right foot, required assistance from a trainer and teammate AJ Swann to reach the injury tent, and later headed to the locker room. He did not return to finish the game. Taylor completed 2 of 5 passes for 10 yards and recorded minus-12 rushing yards on three carries. Backup Parker “Billy” Puckett took over for the remainder of the contest. Taylor was later seen wearing a walking boot. Mississippi State, now 4-3 overall and 2-3 in the SEC, next plays at Texas on October 31, 2026. It remains to be seen whether Kamario Taylor will be playing anytime soon, and what the extent of his injury is. item.title: Ainsley Gump sets new SHS pool record in 200 individual medley
item.description: STURGIS — Ainsley Gump has done it again. On Thursday evening, Sturgis High School's senior swimmer delivered another impressive performance. It came in the 200 individual medley, where Gump registered a new pool record. The previous record was set back in 1999. Her time on Thursday was 2:13.70, which helped Sturgis move past Otsego for a 101-74 victory in the pool. Seniors Katelyn Halling and Lilly Whitehead had first-place finishes to help the Trojans as well. FOOTBALL FRIDAY: Friday recap | Three Rivers beats Sturgis, Mendon scores nearly 100 GUMP NOT DONE YET: Ainsley Gump's SHS career is winding down — but it has not closed just yet Halling recorded first place in the spring events. She swam a time of 26.58 seconds in the 50 freestyle and 59.35 seconds in the 100 freestyle to log winning swims. Whitehead won the 100 breaststroke with a time of 1:16.10. The three Sturgis swimmers joined Brooklyn Draper in the night's opening event, the 200 medley relay, and they swam to victory. Their time was 2:02.18 for first place. That group has already qualified for the MHSAA state finals in that race. Sturgis's win over Otsego pushed the Trojans to 5-5 overall, and they are 4-3 in conference action. Sydney Herblet came in first in the 200 freestyle. Her time of 2:15.83 was just fast enough to beat Morgan Gruber's time from Otsego of 2:16.89. Makenna Holden came in third for Sturgis at 2:50.76, Jazmyne Hunt swam 3:10.98 for fourth. Draper was third in the 200 IM (2:44.16) and Haylee Trine (3:45.04) came in fourth. Whitehead was just behind Halling in the 50 free, swimming a second-place time of 28.03 seconds. In diving, Trine finished third for Sturgis at 104.35 points. Gump won the 100 butterfly at 1:06.53, Mia Feyes was third overall at 1:35.60. In the 100 free, Ava Albarran placed third at 1:10.33, and Alivia Kinsey placed fifth at 1:24.65. Herblet swam to second in the 500 freestyle, her time was 6:02.70. Sturgis won the 200 freestyle relay. The team of Gump, Herblet, Whitehead and Halling posted 1:46.96 to claim victory. Draper's time of 1:11.23 was good for second in the 100 backstroke. Feyes swam to third place in that race at 1:19.15. Albarran was fourth at 1:26.27. For the 400 freestyle, Sturgis finished second. The team of Draper, Albarran, Feyes and Herblet clocked 4:40.80. The team of Holden, Hunt, Kinsey and Chiara Guiduzzi finished third in that event at 5:36.14. item.title: Browns 27 Titans 24 quick recap
item.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 25: Tony Pollard #20 of the Tennessee Titans avoids a tackle from Denzel Ward #21 of the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Nissan Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, at least that was an exciting loss, I guess. The Tennessee Titans will have to wait at least another three weeks to win their first back-to-back wins since 2022 (they have their bye after next week). The Titans got off to a fast start in this one. Tony Pollard ran all over the Browns in the first quarter with two rushing touchdowns on the first two possessions. The second was set up by a Cor’Dale Flott interception of Deshaun Watson. Unfortunately, the Titans wouldn’t score again until Joey Slye kicked a 29-yard field goal with 8:41 left in the fourth quarter. That’s the product of the offense continuing to be inconsistent. That field goal tied the game at 17. After the Browns scored a touchdown to go up 24-17, Cam Ward and the Titans put together an 11-play, 63-yard touchdown drive that ended with Pollard scoring his third touchdown of the day from 1 yard out. The hope was that the game would get to overtime. It did not. The Browns went 55 yards in just 4 plays to set up the game-winning field goal. There was plenty of good in this game. The Titans have a stud in Carnell Tate. He had 5 catches for 69 yards, including a really nice 18-yard catch to set up Pollard’s game-tying touchdown. Now, they just need to find a quarterback who can play consistently enough to sustain an offense for 4 quarters.

item.title: Mark Davis Has Strong Words For Klint Kubiak Amid Losing Streak
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis. Getty Over the years, Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis has cycled through many head coaches. For whatever reason, he hasn’t been able to find the right guy. With how many names he has hired and fired, you would think he’d luck into at least one legitimate head coach. This offseason, the Raiders hired Klint Kubiak, who was previously the offensive coordinator for the Seattle Seahawks. The first three games of his tenure looked excellent, as the team started off 3-0. However, they quickly crashed back to earth and lost three games in a row, dropping to 3-3. Outside of the blowout loss to the New England Patriots in Week 5, the Raiders have remained competitive. The team wasn’t supposed to be good this season, so even being in the mix for the playoffs is a win. Davis has been quick to move on from coaches in the past, but it sounds like he still very much believes in Kubiak. “I think he’s doing a great job,” Davis said of Kubiak in an interview with The New York Post . “He’s building a culture. I have a whole lot of faith in him.” Davis Believes He Has Long-Term Solution Davis has been short on patience. None of the Raiders’ last three head coaches made it to two full seasons in the job. Some may argue that he pivoted too quickly, but he felt he’d rather correct a mistake quickly than double down. “I didn’t feel negatively about anybody, starting out,” Davis said of previous regimes. “It just became very clear that it wasn’t the right fit or the right situation. And I wanted to make the changes quickly enough that it didn’t linger.” This time, Davis feels good about what the team is building. “At this point, I’m very confident that we’ve got a long-term situation to work with,” Davis said. Kubiak Draws Praise From Rams Kubiak has been in the NFL for a while and has called offensive plays for a few teams. He had a hard time finding a long-term home for reasons beyond his control. Los Angeles Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula got to know Kubiak very well last season while he was on the Seahawks, and he thinks highly of the coach. “He was in New Orleans a couple of years ago and you see he does a great job,” Shula said of Kubiak, via Raiders.com . “You can see obviously it’s his offense. You see a lot of the concepts and a lot of the stuff that they did at those places. … I think he does one of the best jobs in the league at matching the offense to the personnel and the skill sets that they have. There are certain things at other places that he would do based on the personnel that they have and there are certain things at the Raiders that he’s doing, obviously with some of the great players with [Brock] Bowers and those great backs that he has. I think he’s one of the best in the league at what he does and it’s a huge challenge.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Mark Davis Has Strong Words For Klint Kubiak Amid Losing Streak appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Browns’ KC Concepcion joins exclusive rookie club since 2000 with only Odell Beckham Jr.
item.description: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images Browns’ KC Concepcion joins exclusive rookie club since 2000 with only Odell Beckham Jr. appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns went into halftime up 17-14 over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. While it’s been a bit of a slow game since the first quarter, first-round pick KC Concepcion was incredibly busy in the first half. So much so that he joins Odell Beckham Jr. in an impressive rookie feat. Reports indicate that Concepcion is the first rookie to record eight or more catches and 125 or more receiving yards in the first half of a game since 2014, according to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN. Beckham is the only other individual to accomplish that feat as a rookie during his first year with the New York Giants. “Browns WR KC Concepcion joined Odell Beckham Jr. as one of 2 rookies since 2000 with 8+ receptions and 125+ receiving yards in the first half of a game (via ESPN Research),” Oyefusi said on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 22-year-old has eight catches for 129 yards off 10 targets through three quarters of play. He’s been Deshaun Watson’s go-to target throughout the game. Especially in the first two quarters, when the Browns got the offense rolling in quarter two. But things have cooled down a tad for Concepcion since coming out of halftime. KC Concepcion entered the Week 7 matchup with 22 receptions for 186 yards off 35 targets. He has yet to score the first touchdown of his career. With Sunday’s contest in the fourth quarter, the former Texas A&M Aggie is running out of time to find pay dirt against the Titans. It’s been a good day for the Browns’ rookie. This appears to be his breakout game, which is a great sign for things to come. item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 22: Joel Embiid #21 of the Philadelphia 76ers and LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers look on during the second quarter against the Cleveland Cavaliers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty Joel Embiid wanted another opportunity to play Sunday night. The Philadelphia 76ers, however, are sticking to their plan. The Sixers officially ruled out Embiid for Sunday’s matchup against the Detroit Pistons, less than 24 hours after the former MVP recorded a triple-double in Philadelphia’s third consecutive victory. According to the NBA’s 1 p.m. ET injury report, Embiid will sit because of right plantar fasciitis management. Meanwhile, LeBron James is not listed on the report, putting him in position to return after missing Saturday’s 127-116 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks. item.title: Cleveland Browns rookie WR hits historic mark against Titans
item.description: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have had several notable wide receivers in franchise history. Dante Lavelli and Mac Speedie in the 1940s and 1950s. Gary Collins and Paul Warfield in the 1960s. Reggie Rucker and Dave Logan in the 1970s. Webster Slaughter, Brian Brennan, and Reggie Langhorne in the 1980s. But very few had a day during their rookie seasons like the one KC Concepcion had on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Concepcion lit up the Titans for 129 receiving yards, a total that puts him at No. 8 on the franchise’s all-time list for receiving yards by a rookie wide receiver in a single game. Derrick Alexander holds the franchise record of 171 yards, set in 1994 in a game against the New York Giants. Concepcion looked to be on track to top Alexander, but just missed a deep pass in the third quarter and was shut out in the entire second half. He still contributed, however, as a key run in the fourth quarter set up a Deshaun Watson touchdown. Unlike Concepcion, Alexander’s record day came in a Week 13 loss as the Browns committed five turnovers and committed 11 penalties. Alexander finished with seven receptions, including a 60-yarder with about five minutes remaining that set up a game-tying touchdown. That was actually one of two big days that season for Alexander, as he had a 136-yard game against the Arizona Cardinals in a Week 3 victory. The new Top 10 for most receiving yards by a Browns rookie, according to statemuse.com , is now: Derrick Alexander, 171 yards in 1994 Mohamed Massaquoi, 148 yards in 2009 Derrick Alexander, 136 yards in 1994 Kevin Johnson, 135 yards in 1999 Webster Slaughter, 134 yards in 1986 Greg Little, 131 yards in 2011 Kevin Johnson, 131 yards in 1999 KC Concepcion, 129 yards in 2026 Paul Warfield, 126 yards in 1964 Paul Warfield 123 yards in 1964 Concepcion now has 30 catches for 315 yards on the season. item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
